desc: Derive and verify the DP state definitions: f(v) = max vertices of a valid partial alkane in subtree(v) where v's parent edge counts as one of v's connections (v is either a leaf: value 1, or internal with exactly 3 selected children: value 1 + sum of f of 3 children), and g(v) = max complete alkane within subtree(v) (either some child's g, or v as degree-4 root with exactly 4 children: 1 + sum of 4 children's f).

Prove that optimal alkane subgraphs can be assumed induced connected subtrees and that each kept internal vertex keeps exactly 4 kept-neighbors, leaves keep 1 — validating that only f/g transitions are needed.

Handle the rerooting/completion subtlety: discovered alkanes whose topmost vertex is a leaf L attached directly to a degree-4 vertex v (v keeps parent edge + 3 children = state3) are missed by state4 alone; answer must also include 1 + state3(v) for every non-root v. Verified on sample 1 (yields 8).

Implement iterative post-order DFS computing per node: gains of children = max(1, state3(child)); state3(v) = 1 + sum of top-3 gains if ≥3 children else -inf; state4(v) = 1 + sum of top-4 gains if ≥4 children else -inf.
Fix final answer: ans = max(state4(v) for all v, 1 + state3(v) for non-root v); print ans or -1. Update code accordingly.
Test edge cases: star K1,4 (answer 5), path (answer -1), sample 2 (-1), samples 1 and 3 (8 and 11), and a case where the best alkane's top is a leaf attached to a state3 node.
Finalize code with fast I/O (sys.stdin.buffer), adjacency lists, iterative stack; confirm complexity O(N log N) worst case.
